solution: Sort the three values so that a <= b <= c. Replacing the largest with a+b gives (a, b, a+b) whose range is b, whereas replacing a or b raises the maximum to b+c or a+c and never helps; moreover (a, b, a+b) reproduces the same situation under the rule, so further operations cannot improve it. The answer is therefore min(c-a, b): either leave the numbers alone or collapse the largest once. This is O(1) per test after ordering three integers. A breadth-first search over every triple with entries 0..12 and up to six operations agrees with the formula everywhere, and all six samples match.
